questions.prompt: A model predicts the settlement of 26 footings (mm) from four predictors: footing width, applied load, soil modulus and depth to groundwater. How many **error degrees of freedom** does the fitted model have?
questions.explanation: n = 26 footings and k = 4 predictors, so p = k + 1 = 5 coefficients are estimated (the intercept too). The error degrees of freedom are n − k − 1 = 26 − 4 − 1 = 21.

questions.prompt: In a fitted model Drying time (min) = b₀ + b₁·Film thickness (µm) + b₂·Humidity (%), what are the units of b₁?
options: Minutes per micrometer of film thickness
Micrometers of film thickness per minute
Minutes per percent of relative humidity
No units, because b₁ is a pure number
questions.explanation: Every term of the equation is in the response's units (minutes), so b₁ × thickness must be in minutes: b₁ is in minutes per µm. b₂ is in minutes per percent of humidity.

questions.prompt: An engineer wants to predict a chiller's daily electricity use **the evening before** from columns in the plant log. Which are sensible candidate predictors? Choose every one that fits.
options: Tomorrow's scheduled number of production shifts
The day's measured chilled-water flow through the plant
A second column with the same forecast converted to °F
questions.explanation: The forecast temperature and the shift schedule are known the evening before and plausibly drive the load. The chilled-water flow is a consequence of the load and is not known in advance. A second column with the temperature in °F is an exact linear function of the temperature in °C, so least squares cannot fit both.

questions.prompt: Which of these is **not** a multiple linear regression model that ordinary least squares can fit as written?
options: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₁² + β₃x₂ + ε
questions.explanation: Linear means linear in the coefficients. √x₁, 1/x and x₁² are just new predictor columns, so the first three are linear models. In the last one β₁ is an exponent, so the model is not linear in its coefficients (taking logs of both sides would make it linear, with ln y as the response).

questions.prompt: Match each part of the model Y = β₀ + β₁X₁ + … + βₖXₖ + ε with what it is.

pairs.right: The mean response when every predictor is 0
The change in mean Y per unit of X₁, others fixed
The number of predictors in the model

questions.explanation: β₀ is the intercept, β₁ … βₖ are the partial regression coefficients (each with the other predictors held fixed), ε is the error term, and k counts the predictors, so the model has k + 1 coefficients.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the error term ε of a multiple regression model is part of the usual assumptions?
options: Its standard deviation is the same at every combination of predictors
Its standard deviation grows in proportion to the fitted value ŷ
Its errors are correlated from one observation to the next
Its values follow a uniform distribution centered on zero
questions.explanation: The LINE assumptions: the mean of Y is linear in the coefficients, the errors are independent, normally distributed, with equal variance σ² everywhere. Module 13 checks them with the residuals.
